working_title: County Down's Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass, and Kirkistown for UK Visitors
angle: County Down is home to one of the world's great links in Royal County Down, but the full circuit including the cliff-top drama of Ardglass and the underrated Ards Peninsula gem of Kirkistown Castle makes for a far richer trip than a single bucket-list round. The post maps out how UK visitors should actually plan and route the trip, including which courses to pair together, realistic booking realities (especially for RCD), and how to get there without flying.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (RCD): located in Newcastle on Dundrum Bay, with the Mourne Mountains as backdrop; 36-hole club comprising Championship Links (par 71, 7,186 yards) and Annesley Links (par 66, ~4,548 yards); founded 1889. Course features towering sand dunes, blind tee shots, gorse-covered sandhills. Consistently ranked among the top five courses in the world.
- RCD visitor access: visitors welcome on designated days (Monday, Tuesday, Thursday mornings, Friday, Sunday afternoons per one source); advance booking essential due to high demand. Several tee shots are blind — a local caddie or course guide is recommended.
- RCD green fees 2026: £450 for Championship Course (peak season, per wanderinggolfers.com and National Club Golfer 2026 survey). Annesley Links considerably cheaper (low season from ~£30, peak ~£45 per 18 holes per one source). Fees have risen significantly year-on-year.
- Ardglass Golf Club: coastal links ~20 miles from RCD; sits on rocky clifftop prominence above the sea; clubhouse reportedly dates to 13th century; routing covers nearly two miles of jagged rocky cliffs. Green fees risen to around £220 peak season in 2025 (per GolfPass); now considered a must-play alongside RCD.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club: links course on eastern shore of Ards Peninsula, Cloughey, County Down; founded 1902, layout shaped by James Braid in 1934; par 69-70, ~6,167 yards; most easterly 18-hole course on the island of Ireland; approximately 45 minutes by road from Belfast. Quick-draining links terrain means rarely closed even after heavy rain — strong year-round option. Green fees approximately £35–£40. Signature hole is the par-4 10th, ~435 yards, with a raised pulpit green, considered one of the hardest par-4s in Irish golf. Recently recognised as Best Value Golf Experience in Ulster (per golfinginireland.org).
- Royal Belfast Golf Club: established 1881, oldest golf club in Ireland; designed by Harry S. Colt; parkland course in Holywood with views of Belfast Lough — worth noting for those based in Belfast.
- Getting there from UK mainland: Belfast has two airports (George Best Belfast City, BHD, and Belfast International, BFS). Ferries from Cairnryan in Scotland and from Liverpool serve Belfast — useful option for UK golfers travelling with own clubs and car. Belfast City Airport is 30–40 minutes from Newcastle, Bangor, or Downpatrick by car. Belfast International is approximately 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes from destinations in County Down.
- Newcastle (the town) is a pleasant seaside base for RCD; Slieve Donard Resort & Spa is the well-known hotel option immediately adjacent to RCD.
- A car is essential for getting around County Down and linking courses together.
- Combining RCD with Ardglass and Kirkistown makes a logical county-wide loop: Newcastle base → RCD Championship + Annesley → Ardglass (20 miles north) → Kirkistown (Ards Peninsula, ~45 mins from Belfast). Three-to-four-day trip feasible for UK visitors.
- Note: sources vary on precise RCD green fees (different third-party sites show different figures); the £450 figure for 2026 peak season comes from National Club Golfer's 2026 survey and wanderinggolfers.com. Do not present any single fee figure as definitive — advise readers to check royalcountydown.org directly before booking.
